title: Medivators Advantage Plus Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Network, Data Export, or Instrument Tracking Interface Failure
description: Addresses missing cycle transfers, export failures, or tracking-interface communication problems caused by cables, network access, destination availability, time, or configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect Traceability and Clinical Workflow
steps.instructions: Use the facility’s approved downtime documentation process when electronic records are not reaching the required tracking system. Do not process endoscopes under incomplete or incorrect identifiers. Confirm that completed cycle data remains available locally before restarting or making changes. Expected outcome: Endoscope traceability is preserved while the communication path is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue affects: All cycle records or selected records One chamber or both Network transmission USB or removable-media export Instrument tracking Patient or endoscope data import Printer output only A single destination or all destinations Record the exact message, time of occurrence, and last known successful transfer. Expected outcome: The affected portion of the communication workflow is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Local Cycle Record Creation
steps.instructions: Check that the AER generated and stored the complete cycle record. Confirm the cycle status, identifiers, date, and time. If the record is absent locally, do not treat the issue as only a network problem. Expected outcome: The source record is present and accurate, allowing the failure to be isolated downstream.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Network Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the Ethernet cable, wall jack, patch connection, or approved network adapter. Look for: Loose connectors Broken locking tabs Damaged cable Pinched routing Connection to the wrong jack Missing link indicators where provided Recent equipment movement Reseat accessible connections and test with a known-good approved cable when available. Expected outcome: The physical network connection is secure. If the known-good cable restores transfer, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Check the Network Outlet or Local Infrastructure
steps.instructions: Confirm whether another approved device can communicate from the same network outlet, or whether the AER communicates when connected to a known-good authorized port. Coordinate with Information Services before moving the AER to a different network segment. Expected outcome: The wall port and local network path are confirmed operational or an infrastructure fault is identified.

steps.title: 6. Check Destination-System Availability
steps.instructions: Determine whether the instrument-tracking server, data repository, interface engine, or receiving application is online. Ask Information Services or the application owner whether other devices are failing to transmit. Avoid repeated retransmission if duplicate records could be created. Expected outcome: The receiving system is available and accepting records, or a broader server/interface outage is confirmed.

steps.title: 7. Verify Date and Time
steps.instructions: Check the AER’s displayed date and time against the facility standard. Significant mismatch can interfere with record matching, certificates, or interface processing. Correct date and time only through authorized settings and facility procedures. Expected outcome: The AER date and time are accurate and consistent with the receiving system.

steps.title: 8. Verify Authorized Communication Settings
steps.instructions: Review visible, approved settings such as selected destination, export mode, network status, or interface enablement. Compare with a working unit or documented configuration. Do not change IP addressing, security settings, certificates, ports, or protected interface parameters without coordination and authorization. Expected outcome: The AER is configured to send data to the intended destination.

steps.title: 9. Test a Controlled Record Transfer
steps.instructions: Use an approved stored record or verification cycle to test the complete path. Confirm the record reaches the correct destination with accurate cycle, operator, endoscope, and time information. Check for queued records and manage duplicates according to policy. Expected outcome: The record transfers correctly and appears at the receiving system. The issue is resolved, and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Stop and Escalate When Communication Remains Unreliable
steps.instructions: If local records, cables, wall ports, time, destination availability, and visible settings are acceptable but communication still fails, escalate jointly to qualified service personnel and Information Services. Do not modify protected network configuration or install unapproved software. Expected outcome: The AER is either removed from service or operated only under an approved documented downtime process.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that Advantage Plus cycle records were stored locally but were not appearing in the instrument-tracking system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the Ethernet cable disconnected from the wall jack after the AER had been moved for floor cleaning.
CCR.Resolution: The cable was reconnected and secured, network status returned, and a verification-cycle record was confirmed at the tracking-system workstation.

title: Medivators Advantage Plus Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Printer or Cycle Record Output Failure
description: Addresses missing, incomplete, faded, or failed cycle records caused by paper, printer power, connections, queue, settings, or external reporting problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Traceability and Reprocessing Records
steps.instructions: Do not discard or release required cycle documentation without following the facility’s approved downtime process. Confirm whether the AER itself shows a successfully completed cycle before addressing only the output problem. Do not interpret a missing printout as proof that the cycle failed or succeeded. Expected outcome: Endoscope traceability is preserved while record output is restored.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Output Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves: No printout Blank paper Faded print Partial record Paper jam Repeated records Wrong cycle information A report that exists electronically but does not print Failure affecting one or all cycles Record any displayed printer or export message. Expected outcome: The problem is separated into printer hardware, media, queue, configuration, or data-generation categories.

steps.title: 3. Verify Cycle Completion and Stored Record
steps.instructions: Check whether the completed cycle appears in the AER’s normal record or history view. Confirm the correct endoscope, operator, date, time, and cycle status. Do not recreate or alter the clinical record merely to produce a printout. Expected outcome: The source cycle record is confirmed as present and accurate, or a broader record-generation problem is identified.

steps.title: 4. Check Printer Power and Status
steps.instructions: Verify that the printer is powered, online, and free of obvious fault indicators. Check its approved power source, power cord, and accessible connection to the AER. If the printer uses a separate outlet, verify that the outlet supports another low-risk test device according to facility practice. Expected outcome: The printer has stable power and is in a ready state.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Paper and Media Loading
steps.instructions: Check that the correct approved paper or media is installed with the proper orientation. Inspect for: Empty roll or tray Incorrect paper type Reversed thermal paper Wrinkled or damp paper Misaligned roll Open cover Paper scraps Visible jam Do not insert tools into the printer mechanism. Expected outcome: Approved media is installed correctly and feeds freely. If proper loading restores printing, continue to verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect External Printer Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect and reseat accessible printer cables only while the devices are safely idle. Look for: Loose connectors Damaged cable insulation Bent pins Strain at the connector Liquid contamination Connection to the wrong port Use a known-good approved cable when available. Expected outcome: The printer connection is secure and undamaged. If a known-good cable restores output, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Check Output Selection and Queue
steps.instructions: Verify that the correct printer or output destination is selected through authorized user settings. Check for a paused printer, accumulated queue, or a record waiting for manual release. Do not change protected network, system, or service configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The intended output destination is active and able to receive the cycle record.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Test Print or Reprint
steps.instructions: Use an approved test-print, stored-record reprint, or nonclinical verification function. Confirm that the printout is complete, legible, and matches the selected record. Avoid creating duplicate clinical documentation without marking or managing it according to policy. Expected outcome: The printer produces a complete and accurate record. The issue is resolved, and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Verify the Full Cycle Record Workflow
steps.instructions: Run the approved verification cycle and confirm: Successful cycle completion Electronic record creation Correct date and time Correct identifiers Complete printed or exported record No printer or communication alarm Expected outcome: The complete documentation pathway functions correctly.

steps.title: 10. Stop and Escalate When Record Output Remains Unreliable
steps.instructions: If paper, power, connections, queue, and output settings are correct but records remain missing or inaccurate, remove the printer function or AER from service as required by facility traceability policy. Do not disassemble the printer or alter protected system configuration without approved documentation. Expected outcome: Reprocessing is not continued without a reliable documentation method.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that completed Advantage Plus cycles were not producing printed records.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external printer powered off after its power strip had been switched off during cleaning.
CCR.Resolution: Printer power was restored, a stored record printed correctly, and a verification cycle generated a complete and legible cycle report.

title: Medivators Advantage Plus Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Rinse Water Quality, Conductivity, or Final Rinse Alarm
description: Addresses final-rinse or water-quality alarms caused by facility water changes, treatment-system problems, expired filters, contamination, flow instability, or sensing faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patients and Reprocessing Workflow
steps.instructions: Treat any endoscope from a cycle stopped by a final-rinse or water-quality alarm as incompletely reprocessed. Quarantine it and use another verified AER when available. Do not bypass the alarm or release the endoscope based only on earlier completed phases. Expected outcome: Endoscopes are not used after an unverified final rinse.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Alarm
steps.instructions: Record the exact message and determine whether it refers to: Rinse water quality Conductivity Final rinse Filter condition Water-treatment status Temperature Flow A specific chamber An intermittent or recurring condition Ask whether the issue began after filter service, plumbing work, sanitation, or a water interruption. Expected outcome: The alarm is accurately categorized before troubleshooting begins.

steps.title: 3. Check for Facility Water Events
steps.instructions: Contact Facilities or review department notices for: Plumbing repairs Water-main work Utility shutdowns Flushing Discoloration Changes in water source Low pressure Water-treatment service Recent return from outage Compare with another AER or water-quality-dependent device on the same supply when appropriate. Expected outcome: A facility-wide water condition is either identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Incoming Water Appearance and Supply Condition
steps.instructions: Where facility procedures permit, check the incoming water source for visible discoloration, sediment, odor, air, or unstable flow. Confirm the supply valve is fully open and the external hose is not kinked. Do not independently sample or certify water quality without approved equipment and procedure. Expected outcome: Incoming water appears normal and reaches the AER without restriction.

steps.title: 5. Review Filter and Water-Treatment Status
steps.instructions: Check documented replacement status for all applicable external and AER-associated water filters. Inspect accessible housings for leaks, incorrect valve alignment, overdue labels, or recent incomplete service. Verify that facility water-treatment equipment serving the AER is operational. Do not bypass filters or treatment stages. Expected outcome: Required filtration and treatment components are in service and within documented status.

steps.title: 6. Check for Recent Filter Replacement or Sanitation
steps.instructions: Determine whether the alarm began immediately after filter replacement, sanitation, plumbing work, or prolonged shutdown. Verify that required flushing, priming, or post-service verification was completed by qualified personnel. Do not reset water-quality warnings without confirming the underlying condition. Expected outcome: Post-service air, residue, or incomplete flushing is identified and corrected through the approved process.

steps.title: 7. Verify Drain and Flow Conditions
steps.instructions: Check that the chamber drains fully and incoming flow is stable. Retained fluid, poor drainage, or inconsistent filling can affect the final-rinse process and may appear as a water-quality alarm. Inspect external supply and drain hoses for restriction. Expected outcome: The AER fills, circulates, and drains normally without mixing or retention caused by an external restriction.

steps.title: 8. Check Environment and Chemical Storage
steps.instructions: Confirm that detergent, disinfectant, and other approved consumables are correctly connected and not leaking into the wrong area. Inspect for spilled chemical near water connections or filter housings. Do not attempt to neutralize or flush chemical contamination without an approved procedure. Expected outcome: No visible chemical cross-contamination or incorrect consumable connection is present.

steps.title: 9. Perform Approved Water-System Verification
steps.instructions: After external utilities, filters, treatment equipment, and post-service steps are confirmed, run the approved empty-cycle, rinse, or water-system verification process. Observe for: Stable fill Normal circulation Complete drainage No final-rinse alarm No conductivity or water-quality warning Successful cycle completion Expected outcome: The AER accepts the rinse-water condition and completes the verification cycle. The issue is resolved, and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Stop and Escalate When Water Quality Cannot Be Verified
steps.instructions: If the facility supply, filters, treatment system, flow, drainage, and consumable connections are acceptable but the alarm remains, remove the AER from service. Do not adjust conductivity calibration, bypass sensors, or access internal water-quality components without approved manufacturer procedures. Expected outcome: The AER is prevented from processing endoscopes until final-rinse quality can be reliably verified.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported repeated final-rinse water-quality alarms on the Advantage Plus after facility plumbing work.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering and Facilities found sediment loading in the external pretreatment filter following restoration of the water supply.
CCR.Resolution: Facilities replaced the approved pretreatment filter, the supply was flushed according to procedure, and the AER completed the required verification cycle without water-quality alarms.

title: Medivators Advantage Plus Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Touchscreen Unresponsive or Software Freeze
description: Addresses frozen screens, delayed touch response, or software lockups caused by contamination, power interruption, peripheral faults, environmental conditions, or software problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patients and Reprocessing Workflow
steps.instructions: If the touchscreen freezes during a cycle, treat the cycle as incomplete unless the AER clearly completes and records it according to the validated process. Quarantine the endoscope and move work to another verified AER. Do not disconnect power while chemical movement, draining, or an active cycle may still be occurring unless an emergency requires it. Expected outcome: The affected endoscope and staff remain protected while the equipment state is assessed.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The display is visible but touch does not respond Only one screen area is unresponsive The image is frozen The system is slow Physical controls also fail A cycle continues in the background The unit restarts repeatedly The problem occurs after a specific screen or action Record all displayed messages before attempting a restart. Expected outcome: The failure is characterized as a touch-input, display, software, or broader power condition.

steps.title: 3. Check Whether a Cycle Is Active
steps.instructions: Observe status indicators, pump sounds, fluid movement, alarms, and any connected printer or record output. Do not open the chamber or interrupt utilities solely because the display appears frozen. Follow the approved emergency or interrupted-cycle procedure if the AER state cannot be determined. Expected outcome: The unit’s operating state is identified without creating a chemical or reprocessing hazard.

steps.title: 4. Inspect and Clean the Touchscreen Surface
steps.instructions: Check for: Water or chemical residue Gloves or covers interfering with touch Adhesive film Cracks Impact damage Heavy contamination An object pressing against the display Clean and dry the screen using an approved method. Expected outcome: The touchscreen surface is clean, dry, undamaged, and free of physical interference. If touch response returns, continue to verification.

steps.title: 5. Check External Peripherals
steps.instructions: Disconnect only approved removable peripherals that are not required for safe operation, such as an external barcode scanner or printer, after the unit is safely idle. A failed peripheral or cable can sometimes affect software response. Do not disconnect network, chemical, water, or internal connections as a diagnostic shortcut. Expected outcome: A faulty external peripheral is isolated, or the screen remains frozen with peripherals removed.

steps.title: 6. Verify Stable Power
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord, plug, strain relief, outlet, and any approved power-distribution device. Check for evidence of recent power interruption, loose plugs, tripped circuits, or facility electrical work. Do not continue using an AER that loses power unpredictably. Expected outcome: The AER has a secure and stable power source.

steps.title: 7. Perform an Authorized Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: Once the cycle state is safe and the affected endoscope remains quarantined, use the normal shutdown or restart sequence. Avoid repeated forced power cycles. Observe startup for error messages, unusual delays, or recurrence of the freeze. Expected outcome: The AER starts normally and the touchscreen responds across the full display. If it freezes again, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Check Environment and Ventilation
steps.instructions: Verify that external vents are unobstructed and the room is not unusually hot, cold, or humid. Look for condensation, nearby steam sources, blocked airflow, or heat-producing equipment. Do not open service panels to cool the unit. Expected outcome: The AER operates in a stable environment with unobstructed ventilation.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Full Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Test the touchscreen across normal authorized screens and run the approved empty or verification cycle. Confirm: Reliable touch response Normal screen transitions No software freeze Correct alarm acknowledgment Complete cycle progression Accurate cycle record Expected outcome: The touchscreen and software remain stable through the complete test. The issue is resolved, and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Stop and Escalate When Freezing Recurs
steps.instructions: If the touchscreen is clean, power is stable, peripherals are ruled out, and environmental conditions are acceptable but the freeze returns, remove the AER from service. Do not access internal computing hardware, reinstall software, or use unauthorized service tools. Expected outcome: An AER with unreliable controls is prevented from processing endoscopes.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the Advantage Plus touchscreen stopped responding at the cycle-selection screen.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried chemical residue along the lower edge of the touchscreen, causing continuous false touch input.
CCR.Resolution: The screen was cleaned and dried using the approved method, and the AER completed a full verification cycle with reliable touch response and no freeze.
